headline: BULLISH
headline_tag: uptrend intact, but long-term trend still repairing

action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The uptrend is intact, so the current posture supports increasing acquisition budget, with emphasis on active-trader channels that tend to respond most in this phase. Confidence is medium rather than high because the longer-term trend is still recovering and price is well below its previous peak, so a staged increase fits better than a single large one. This is budget-posture guidance based on trailing data, not trading advice.

reasons: Price is 18% above its 200-day average, and 90-day gain is about 40%.
Weekly RSI near 60 shows firm momentum without overbought conditions.
The 200-day average is still falling (-5.3% over 90 days), limiting conviction.
Price remains 33% below its all-time high; Fear & Greed is 73.
watch: The key tension is between fast recent gains and a slow-moving long-term trend: price is up about 40% in 90 days and above its 200-day average, yet that average is still declining and only 47% of recent days closed above it. If the 200-day slope turns flat or positive and breadth broadens, the uptrend read would be better supported; if price slips back under the 200-day average, the read would weaken. These are trailing measures, not forecasts.
analysis: Sentiment is warm but not stretched: Fear & Greed reads 73 (Greed), yet funding is only marginally positive (z-score +0.10) and long positions outnumber shorts by a modest 1.36 to 1. Open interest of about $7.7B, an options-implied volatility (DVOL) of 35.9 and a VIX of 16.1 all point to a calm, not euphoric, backdrop, with realised volatility sitting mid-range at the 50th percentile.

Momentum is the strongest part of the picture: BTC is up roughly 40% over 90 days, weekly RSI is a healthy 60 without being overbought, and the 50/200-day average gap of +8.0% sits on the bullish side. Participation is less convincing, though, with under half (47%) of recent days closing above the 200-day average. ETFs added about $31M on the day, and the next FOMC meeting on 2026-10-27 is the nearest scheduled macro event.

On the long view, price is 18% above its 200-day average (Mayer Multiple 1.18) and 1.28x its 200-week average, but the 200-day line itself is still sloping down (-5.3% over 90 days) and price remains 33% below its all-time high, so this reads as a recovery rather than a mature bull. Macro is a mixed backdrop, with the 10-year yield at 5.24% against a 3.63% fed funds rate, while cumulative ETF inflows of roughly $57.6B and about 1.28M BTC held by public companies show sustained institutional holding.
